title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
abstract: For a general entanglement-assisted or unassisted quantum error-correcting code, a set of erasures, and an associated repair group, we propose a linear algebraic procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The procedure has cubic complexity in the repair group size and the computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures. We specialize the general procedure to quantum codes constructed from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and provide closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for those special cases. Based on these closed-form bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the information locality of classical local recovery.
summary: This paper presents a novel linear algebraic method to optimize quantum error correction by simultaneously minimizing the necessary observables and the measured qudits for correcting erasures. It provides rigorous procedures and bounds for general entanglement-assisted quantum codes. This work advances the theoretical understanding of resource reduction in quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper develops a linear algebraic procedure to simultaneously reduce the set of observables and the measured qudits required for quantum error correction when correcting erasures in entanglement-assisted quantum local recovery.
main_result: The proposed procedure computes a reduced set of observables of minimum possible size and a reduced repair group, providing closed-form upper bounds for specific code constructions.
method: The core method is a linear algebraic procedure involving subspace decomposition, rank calculations, and greedy column reduction to minimize the required measurement resources.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs), particularly entanglement-assisted codes defined over $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$, addressing the challenge of quantum erasure correction.
key_observables: The size of the reduced observable set ($|O|$) and the size of the reduced repair group ($|J|$).
important_parameters: Code length ($n$), field size ($q$), the size of the initial repair group ($|K|$), and the size of the erasure set ($|I|$).
main_assumptions: The procedure is specialized for general EAQECCs, though initial derivations rely on assumptions about the structure of the code and its dual.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general problem, details the linear algebraic procedure for reduction, specializes this procedure to Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality cases, and concludes by deriving and analyzing the resulting upper bounds.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract coding theory, the concepts of local recovery and minimizing measurement overhead are crucial for designing practical quantum communication protocols and fault-tolerant quantum computation.
